notes.title: UPDATE 0.3 - SPIRIT OF A NATION
notes.notes: [p][b]Greetings, dear players of Flames in Modern Europe! I’m glad to announce that the largest update so far has just been released – version 0.3: The Nation Code! [/b][/p][p][b]The focus of this update was on adding new mechanics and improving gameplay. It brings much larger and more significant changes compared to previous updates and touches on every aspect of the game in one way or another.[/b][/p][p][/p][p]This update drastically changes the game, adding many new gameplay elements, mechanics, graphical improvements, and—very importantly—optimizations. Here I will briefly outline the main changes, and below you can read the full changelog.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Mentality Mechanic[/b][/p][p]The game now has a brand-new feature – the mentality mechanic. You can find it in the state menu by pressing the “Our Mentality” button.[/p][p]Mentality traits mainly affect different modifiers, in particular the growth of stability, corruption, tax efficiency, and ruling party support. [/p][p]All countries already have certain mentality traits at the start of the game, but they are not always positive. Fortunately, you can not only research new ones but also remove your existing ones. However, this process takes quite some time, since people cannot be changed overnight...[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45311226/798650ea24f72c2bdc70df3d5ff0611b423c6e84.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][b]Regional Population[/b][/p][p]Back in the demo version you could already see the population of your country, and it was quite dynamic thanks to stability. However, it was calculated as one total number for the whole country, which caused problems when playing as, say, Transnistria or Luxembourg, since conquering new territories didn’t increase population.[/p][p]Now, a huge file with the population of all regions has been filled in, and you can finally see the population of each region in its respective menu. This makes the gameplay much more engaging.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Wars Between AI Countries[/b][/p][p]Previously, the game world was rather static: the player could attack other states, but nothing much happened globally. Now, AI-controlled countries will declare wars on each other depending on the aggression level set at the start of a new game. AI will also create armies from the very beginning, and in case of war, it will mobilize and later demobilize. Incredible changes in the world are already waiting for you! [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45311226/a4a577e2a701938d09e5c055bd63afdbd407ac1e.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Graphics Improvements[/b][/p][p]This is probably a regular part of each update, but this time the graphics have improved significantly.[/p][p]First, the map has become much more volumetric thanks to updated shader normals. This makes it more beautiful and even “tastier.”[/p][p]Second, borders have been reworked. This applies to both their color (previously state borders were light, now they are dark) and their logic—they are now much more precise, fixing a bug with displaying borders of some provinces.[/p][p]Smooth borders have also been greatly improved—you can now choose the degree of smoothing in the menu![img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45311226/851613f6c908961a9434e2a7c3176dcac98892d6.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Optimization and Modding[/b][/p][p]The game engine has been updated to Unity 6.1 to improve performance and speed. A large number of scripts have also been rewritten to enhance optimization.[/p][p]And the most exciting part of this section—players can now write their own localization for mods and add custom sprites![/p][p][/p][p][b]Below you can see the full list of changes:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Added new mentality mechanic [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Population transferred to regions [/p][/*][*][p]Ability to cancel planned construction[/p][/*][*][p]Wars between AI countries[/p][/*][*][p]Reworked “status quo” peace treaty, sped up this event dozens of times[/p][/*][*][p]Peace treaties between AI countries[/p][/*][*][p]AI countries can now demobilize after war[/p][/*][*][p]Reworked brigade-related scripts for significant optimization and improved combat logic [/p][/*][*][p]Ability to destroy encircled armies[/p][/*][*][p]Army destruction without manpower[/p][/*][*][p]Map border quality settings replacing old smooth borders[/p][/*][*][p]Highlighting of selected province on the map[/p][/*][*][p]New events, especially related to new functions in the game[/p][/*][*][p]Rebalanced stability changes from administrative expenses[/p][/*][*][p]Ability to mod localization[/p][/*][*][p]Ability to mod icons[/p][/*][*][p]Game engine updated to Unity 6.1[/p][/*][*][p]Added Mac OS support[/p][/*][*][p]Border highlighting replaced with darkening for a better map look[/p][/*][*][p]Added normal map texture for the world map, greatly improving its quality[/p][/*][*][p]Other shader improvements[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed textures of various 3D objects, including armored vehicles[/p][/*][*][p]GPU optimization[/p][/*][*][p]FPS cap settings[/p][/*][*][p]Changed main cursor[/p][/*][*][p]UI improvements, added beautiful glow effects in various places[/p][/*][*][p]Reworked state menu[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed bug where AI sometimes didn’t create brigades[/p][/*][*][p]Manpower now updates in real time to prevent exploits[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Reworked map shader to increase border detection accuracy[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Brigade models now spawn at different angles[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Added clock to in-game menu[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Fixed settings menu during gameplay[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced game size[/p][/*][*][p]Now you must both own and control a region to create troops[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed volume settings bug[/p][/*][*][p]Other bug fixes[/p][/*][*][p]Automatic language detection on first launch[/p][/*][*][p]Massive optimization of state and army scripts, greatly improving performance and reducing CPU load[/p][/*][*][p]And much notes.title: Update 0.2 – the first major update!
notes.notes:
[p]I’m excited to announce the biggest update so far is now live! This update brings major graphical improvements, powerful optimizations, deeper gameplay complexity — and much more![/p][p]
[/p][p]Originally, this update was meant to only add parliamentary elections... but it quickly grew into a complete overhaul of the map shader, camera (again 🫠), and textures![/p][p]
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45311226/050b85a8986a52c26a3165a758d2c9c04fd0dca2.png"][/img]🗺 Honestly, I can’t imagine how we used to play before this. Now the map is truly stunning — even at maximum zoom! 🤩[/p][p]Previously, the game used a 12K resolution terrain texture. It looked decent from afar, but as you zoomed in, the blurriness became very noticeable. Now the game uses a completely different technology — even on the lowest settings, the terrain stays perfectly sharp! 🥳[/p][p]
[/p][p]📸 Naturally, this required a camera update as well, allowing for much greater zoom-in. In the future, zoom range might be expanded even further.[/p][p]
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45311226/07afe653ff84386eb837094a280dd31c63dcbc6b.png"][/img][/p][p]
[/p][p]I’ve also started investing financially in the game — this update includes paid integration of FSR. Players with weaker GPUs will greatly benefit: instead of lowering resolution to improve FPS, they can now just turn on FSR! It can also be used on native resolution as a high-quality anti-aliasing solution, which the game was lacking until now. ✍️[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45311226/90c3fd65b9f39c9fb8f95d617ac8ac555fa2638c.png"][/img][/p][p]
[/p][p]Visual effects like region highlighting have been reworked as well — it makes a huge difference to immersion. That glow... simply breathtaking 😍[/p][p]
[/p][p]As I mentioned before, regular Parliamentary Elections are now in the game. But no less important are the new Presidential Elections! These take place in two rounds, where parties can endorse candidates from other parties between rounds. A new UI has been added to view candidates — this is only available during the campaign period, which starts two months before the first round.[/p][p]
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45311226/0fe8a2b0ad04fc77685c4b5ef1b468f581c18b41.png"][/img]Nuclear weapons have become even more terrifying... and unforgettable. Literally! Thermonuclear strikes now not only destroy all buildings, but — just like regular nukes — leave permanent visual marks on the map. 🤯[/p][p]
[/p][p]Armies have also evolved, and more improvements are coming. This update introduces several new features: First — the Frontline System is now functional. While you won’t see visual lines just yet, the underlying logic is already implemented.[/p][p]
[/p][p]Second — full-scale invasion. It’s very simple: click one button, choose a target country, and your army marches in! Pure satisfaction... unless you’re the one being invaded. Especially now that your opponents can also deploy up to 50 brigades — thanks to the massive optimization work I’ve done recently.[/p][p]
[/p][p]Last but not least — brigade movement arrows. Veterans will remember the ugly red "stick" from the first gameplay teaser — a clumsy, floating line between provinces. That’s now a thing of the past. Just check the final image in this post to see how clean and stylish it looks now. I really love the result.[/p][p]
[/p][p][/p][p]
[/p][p][b]Here’s the full changelog of this update:[/b][/p][p]
[/p][list][*][p][b]The map shader has been completely reworked[/b] — Europe now looks amazing even at maximum zoom[/p][p][b]The old 12K terrain texture has been replaced[/b] with new tech that removes blurriness even on low settings[/p][p][b]Maximum camera zoom increased[/b] — you can now inspect the terrain much more closely[/p][p][b]FSR support added[/b] — massive FPS boost for players with weaker GPUs. Also works as high-quality anti-aliasing at native resolution[/p][p][b]Visual effects have been redesigned[/b] — especially region highlighting[/p][p][b]Construction icons have been updated[/b] — now fully colored. Further UI improvements in this area are coming soon.[/p][p][b]Brigade movement arrows fully reworked[/b] — old red "sticks" replaced with clean and bright arrows[/p][p][b]Nuclear and thermonuclear weapons now leave permanent visual marks on the map[/b][/p][p][b]Thermonuclear weapons completely destroy all buildings in the region[/b][/p][p][b]Frontline system added[/b] — functional logic implemented, though still invisible visually[/p][p][b]Full-scale invasion option added[/b] — allows a general to order total offensive into enemy territory[/p][p][b]AI opponents now create dozens of brigades[/b] — scale enabled by deep optimization[/p][p][b]Regular Parliamentary Elections added[/b] — in the future, this will be central to political gameplay[/p][p][b]Regular Presidential Elections added[/b] — includes two rounds with vote transfers between parties. Candidates can be viewed during campaign via a button above Parliament[/p][p][b]Construction cost rebalance[/b] — an important economic tweak that increases difficulty[/p][p][b]UI improvements across various menus[/b] — especially the general's interface[/p][p][b]Critical bugs fixed[/b] — including some that existed since the demo[/p][p][b]Fixed a major bug that broke construction until the end of the game[/b][/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Update 0.1.5 – North African Countries and Alliances!
notes.notes:
[b]UPDATE v0.1.5[/b]

[b]Major Map Changes[/b]
• Added countries of the Middle East and North Africa. These territories are now fully playable.

[b]Map Technical Overhaul:[/b]
• Improved visibility of map edges when zoomed out (Ireland, Portugal, Northern Scandinavia, Africa, etc.).
• Managing countries near the edges is now significantly easier.

[b]New Mechanic: Alliances[/b]
New map mode – Alliance Map (toggle with F9):
• Countries can create, leave, and join alliances.
• Joint wars with allies are now possible.
• Financial aid between allies (through the diplomacy menu).

[b]Diplomacy Improvements[/b]
• Key diplomatic actions like improving relations, accusations, and financial aid now have cooldowns.
• Tooltips added to the diplomacy menu.

[b]Fixes to Known Bugs (as of now)[/b]

notes.title: Major Bug & Crash Fixes – Patch 0.1.1!
notes.notes:
[b]Hello everyone![/b]

[b]I sincerely thank each of you for your feedback, patience, and support. [b]Today, I want to share an important update that addresses key issues you've reported since the release.[/b][/b]

Many players experienced game crashes—most often due to weak graphics cards or TDR (Timeout Detection and Recovery) settings. Of course, this couldn’t be ignored. Although I planned to work on new content, guides, and a trailer after release, my main focus was on identifying and fixing the root causes of these crashes.

And here’s the good news! I’m happy to report that [b]from now on, the game will launch stably on any device that meets the minimum requirements![/b] The map initialization logic has been rewritten, province processing optimized, and error protection at startup improved.

[b]Another major improvement is support for monitors of various formats.[/b] Some users with ultrawide monitors had issues so severe that they couldn’t even access the settings to switch to windowed mode. As of now, the game supports nearly all monitor formats, including not just UI adaptation but also camera adaptation. Further improvements are still planned.

Speaking of the camera—the script has been completely redesigned! You can now zoom in right to the map surface, with terrain taken into account!

[b]Additionally, other bugs you reported have been fixed—including the bug with brigades not showing under generals. A large number of “anarchic” provinces have also been fixed.[/b]

This update is just the beginning. I’m already working on upcoming patches and enhancements that will make the game even better, deeper, and more engaging.

[b]Thank you for staying with us. You are the heart of this project.[/b]

[i]Volodymyr Marsenko[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45311226/5ff3fc152c3740f60dceb1d3c7a3624a040e82a9.png[/img]

notes.title: Release in Early Access in just a week!
notes.notes:
Dear players and followers of Flames in Modern Europe!

[b]Today, I am pleased to officially announce an exceptionally important piece of news: the game’s Early Access release is set for just one week from now — on April 21 at 8:00 AM Seattle time (4:00 PM London time)![/b]

This is truly a milestone event for the entire FIME project, which I have been working on for a very long time — and we have all been eagerly awaiting this moment.

In Early Access, you will have the opportunity to be among the first to experience the full gameplay: play as any European country, manage their economic development, diplomatic relations, military conflicts, and political reforms. And this is just the beginning — ahead lies a wealth of updates, new mechanics, and expansions that I plan to develop together with you, taking your feedback and suggestions into account.

FIME is not just a game — it’s a community of like-minded people who are jointly creating a unique Ukrainian project about modern Europe. Your feedback, ideas, and proposals will become an important guide for the future development of the game. It is you who will help shape what FIME will become tomorrow.

On this occasion, I encourage everyone to subscribe to our official pages on Telegram, Instagram, and other social networks — because very soon there will be giveaways of free copies of the game! You’ll also find exclusive announcements, news about upcoming updates, and direct communication with the developer.

I sincerely thank each and every one of you who has been following the project, supporting it, and inspiring further work. Stay with us — the most exciting is yet to come!

[i]Volodymyr Marsenko
Lead Developer of FIME[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45311226/3edfae850228958bacdbd7d421a47ea7c77655ae.png[/img]

notes.title: The demo version of Flames of Modern Europe has been released!
notes.notes:
Today is an important day - the Flames in Modern Europe demo is finally out! This is the first step towards a full release, and I, as the main and only developer, am looking forward to your feedback and sharing it on social media.

This is the first step, but not the last. I can't tell you the exact date of the game's release for pre-access yet - maybe in March, or maybe in April. But we will definitely go through this difficult path together.

The game is also participating in Steam Next Fest, which is starting right now! This is a great opportunity to support the project, try the demo, and help it become even better.

Download, test, and share your impressions! Your support is very important to me. 


Thank you for being with FIME!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45311226/70307382e77ee083b47bd82115e9f17698cfc766.png[/img]

notes.title: Happy New Year!
notes.notes:
Dear awaiting and future players of Flames in Modern Europe! 

As the developer of FIME, I sincerely wish you a belated Merry Christmas and a Happy New Year! This year has been very challenging for all of us, but also rich in important events, including the announcement of Flames in Modern Europe! 

I am proud to say that thanks to your support, the game is constantly being developed, filled with mechanics, and becoming better. You inspire us to achieve new heights and give us the strength to work even harder. 

In the new year, on February 24th, you'll be able to play the free demo version of the game! But before that moment, we still have a difficult path ahead. Therefore, I kindly ask you to add Flames in Modern Europe to your wishlist, share the game with your friends, and follow our community and social media. 

May 2025 bring you lots of joy, health, success, and unforgettable experiences! I wish you peaceful skies, the realization of your dreams, and a great mood every day. 

Thank you for being with FIME!
